North Dakota--The State Planning Division reports the statement is in general conformance with the goals and objectives of the State and is not in conflict with any other State plan on file.
Oregon--Evaluation is embodied in comments of the Oregon State Game

Commission. They feel there is little need for new legislation, that the
only two essential new features of the proposed legislation (1) removal of
the land acquisition ceiling and (2) Secretarial control of the taking of
animals on the high seas by U.S. subjects could be provided by amendment of
the present authority. The Commission protests a stronger Federal role in
the management of endangered species within the States.
Rhode Island--Sees no adverse environmental impact and predic s that economic impacts will be minor and tend to be offset by gains.
South Carolina--Generally favorable response especially by three Regional Planning Councils. The Forestry Commission expresses some concern for Forest resources tied up in tracts set aside for endangered species habitat.
Texas--Generally supports the legislation but concludes with "So much of the bill and statement supporting it we could endorse but not the removal from State jurisdiction of indigenous wildlife forms.
<u>Virginia</u>--Clearinghouse reports no conflict between the proposed legislation and present State law.
Washington--Response embodied in comment by four State agencies which clearly support the statement and the legislation. Three of the Departments express concern about the States' management role--Federal usurpation of State authority.
